Subject: Marketplace page — draft hero + customer scenarios (please review)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the help. Attached is our first draft of the AWS Marketplace product page (hero, 3 usage scenarios, and billing blurb). Can you and your Marketplace team skim the hero headline and the usage examples for field accuracy and co-sell positioning? We especially want to avoid any claims that could be problematic during listing review.

Quick asks:
- Redline any copy that overstates scale or compliance.
- Suggest a 1-line alternative hero and one-sentence usage bullets.
- Confirm whether the trial CTA language is Marketplace-compliant.

Attachment: acme_marketplace_draft.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Erin Walsh

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace page — draft hero + customer scenarios (please review)

Hi Erin — thanks for the draft. Quick skim below and attached a track-changes doc.

High level:
- Hero: remove "instantly" and replace with "fast"; avoid performance promises.
- Usage bullets: tighten to concrete examples (e.g., "automate routing for 10K daily shipments" -> "automate routing for daily shipments at scale")
- Trial CTA: Marketplace requires "Start a free trial" not "Request trial" for standard listings.

I've attached redlines: redwood_hero_edit_v1.docx

If that looks good I'll loop in Marissa for final UX copy polish and HubSpot metadata. Can we aim to sign off by EOD Monday?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Marketplace Programs Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Thanks Kim — pushed more punchy alternatives. Inline highlights below and in the attached copy file.

Hero alternatives (pick one):
- "Cost-efficient LLM inference for production applications"
- "Enterprise-ready inference that balances latency and cost"

Usage bullets (one-sentence):
- "Automate routing decisions for logistics workflows to reduce manual exceptions."
- "Generate real-time customer communications during shipment events."
- "Embed predictive ETA recommendations in driver apps."

Note on evidence: avoid percentage claims unless Acme can provide a verified case study. If they can, we'll add a short evidence callout.
